1. The plan's central factual claim is wrong: dogfood-close_test.sh is THREE sections, not two. Section C (line 643, case C1) tests the SAME live pre-push hook as Section B - that the bd block does not consume stdin and the classifier still sees the buffered refs, the subtlest property of the hook. The plan says extract Section B and delete the rest, and makes its verification 'all ten B-cases', so a coder following it literally deletes C1 and every stated check still goes green - the exact silent coverage regression the plan exists to prevent, one level down.

2. The extraction's dependencies are understated in a way that can make the extracted suite pass while wired to nothing. B and C also depend on the bd PATH shim (lines 106-121, BD_SHIM plus export PATH), defined in the Section A setup region; without it the suite runs against the real bd, C1 stops proving anything and B cases can be masked by a non-zero bd exit. The stated negative control does not cover this - a shim-less copy would still fail against a deliberately broken refs/etude/* branch.
